name: Ribosome Extract (lifecycle-driven template extraction)
description: Activity-driven implementation of the ribosome pattern. Subscribes to lifecycle:activity:postExecution and treats template extraction as a shape-identifying counterpart to goal/activity — input shape lifecycle:activity:postExecution, output shapes extractedTemplate / learningSummary / goalEnd. Replaces the imperative ribosome calls that previously fired inline from activity.ts (recordExecutionTrace path), goal-processor.ts (4 sites: success extraction, cost-limit attempt, LLM-verified attempt, max-turns attempt), and improviser-resolver.ts (success + cost-limit paths). The chain has six tasks: (1) acquire_trace_signature — impulse-resolve `executionTraceWithSignatures` keyed by the just-completed executionId; (2) assess_quality — llm computes a quality score from the lifecycle payload + trace signature (success rate, task count, resolver tier mix, cost-per-output ratio, depth=0 check, author-skip check); (3) gate_extraction — conditional branch on qualityScore >= qualityThreshold; (4) synthesize_template — llm renders an extractedTemplate JSON proposal from the trace signature + lifecycle payload; (5) validate_proposal — llm validates the proposal against compliance rules (similar to replace-activity::validate_proposals); (6) dispatch_write — impulse-resolve with pointer.type=`activityTemplate_write` operation=`create`, GATED on the applyExtraction variable (default false). The applyExtraction default of false makes first-canary-deploy observe-only: the chain emits an extractedTemplate proposal impulse for downstream consumers (workbench, replace-activity, operator) without actually persisting the new template. Once enough proposal traces accumulate and the quality threshold is calibrated, applyExtraction can be flipped to true (per-template variable override) for autonomous registration. RECURSION SAFETY: this template's templateAuthor on the lifecycle payload is `ribosome-pattern`, so when the meta-activity itself emits postExecution at completion, the gate_extraction conditional skips because templateAuthor is matched against a documented skip list (the meta-activity sets `templateAuthor != ribosome-pattern && templateAuthor != ribosome && templateAuthor != ribosome-sequence` as the recursion-safety filter). MIGRATION TARGET: the imperative ribosome calls reach for mcp.registerTemplate(); the meta-activity uses the activityTemplate_write resolver advertised by activity-api per docs/impulse-types/LEARNING_LOOP_WRITE_RESOLVERS.md (post auth fix). Per the system's foundational model: ribosome is the shape-identifying counterpart to goal/activity — runs after execution, registered to the lifecycle hook, declarative quality gates expressed in template variables not buried in code.

variables.name: qualityThreshold
variables.description: Minimum quality score (0-1) required for synthesize_template to fire. Mirrors the imperative call's threshold of 0.6 (activity.ts:3586) but raised slightly to compensate for the meta-activity's broader applicability — the imperative call only ran on shouldExtractTemplate-passing executions, while the lifecycle subscriber receives every postExecution. The acquired trace signature drives the score in assess_quality.

variables.name: applyExtraction
variables.description: When true, dispatch_write task fires `activityTemplate_write` to persist the synthesized template. Default false makes first-canary-deploy observe-only — the chain emits an extractedTemplate proposal impulse for downstream consumers (workbench, replace-activity, operator) without actually writing. Mirrors make-activity.json::applyTemplateExtraction (default false). Once quality calibration converges, flip per-invocation OR per-vessel as a variable override.

variables.name: synthesisMaxTokens
variables.description: Token budget for synthesize_template's LLM call. The synthesized template payload is bounded — per the existing `extractTemplateFromImprovisation` helper in template-extractor.ts, the typical payload is ~1500 tokens for a 3-5 task template. 2000 leaves headroom; raise for richer templates (longer descriptions, more tasks) and lower for token-cost optimization.

variables.name: lifecycle
variables.description: Set automatically by the lifecycle dispatcher (see activity.ts:1249-1273) to the lifecycle:activity:postExecution payload merged with {executionId, shape}. Contains (post-2026-04-27 ribosome refactor): executionId, templateId, templateName, templateAuthor, status, durationMs, costUsd, taskCount, impulseCount, depth, compositionChain (array → JSON-stringified), outputShapes (array → JSON-stringified), hasGoalContext (boolean → string `"true"`/`"false"`), qualityEligible (boolean → string). Dotted-path interpolation works: `{{lifecycle.executionId}}`, `{{lifecycle.templateAuthor}}`, etc. The interpolator was extended to /\{\{([\w]+(?:\.[\w]+)*)\}\}/g in activity.ts iter 7 (slot-binding/validator-dispatch shipped on this primitive). Resolvers can also read the lifecycle:activity:postExecution impulse content directly via `impulses` (delivered as the first impulseRef) for any field not surfaced as a dotted-path placeholder.

tasks.description: Fetch the just-completed execution's trace signature via the canonical executionTraceWithSignatures shape advertised by activity-api (see config.ts:223).
tasks.notes: Uses the existing generic `impulse-resolve` resolver in minibob — zero source changes in the integrating vessel (vessel-integration constraint per shape-provider-goal.json pattern). The signature shape is context-budget-conscious: per-impulse pointer/shape signatures, per-task input/output_impulse_ids, status, duration, resolver tier mix — enough for downstream quality scoring + template synthesis without echoing full trace bodies. SHORT-CIRCUIT (recursion safety): when the lifecycle payload's `templateAuthor` is `ribosome`, `ribosome-pattern`, or `ribosome-sequence`, the conditional skips this task — and the rest of the chain via dependency-skip propagation — so the meta-activity does not extract from its own (or another ribosome activity's) executions. The imperative path used the same skip pattern (activity.ts:3525-3526). Substring-match idiom (used by slot-binding.json:162, goal-processing-activity-driven.json:162) — checks the lifecycle:activity:postExecution impulse content for the literal `"templateAuthor":"ribosome"` etc. SHORT-CIRCUIT (quality gate): when qualityEligible is `false` (lifecycle payload — mirrors the executor's `shouldExtractTemplate` thresholds: completed AND >= 2 tasks AND cost < $1 AND impulses <= 10 AND depth = 0), skip the whole chain. The qualityEligible flag is computed in activity.ts at the postExecution emit site so the meta-activity can short-circuit without re-running the same boolean here.

tasks.description: LLM computes a quality score (0-1) from the trace signature + lifecycle payload.
tasks.notes: Mirrors the imperative `scoreTemplateQuality` in template-generator.ts:885 — checks task count, resolver tier mix (deterministic > pattern > llm), cost-per-output ratio, depth, output-shape diversity, AND the recursion-safety filter (templateAuthor must NOT be in the ribosome family). Returns a structured JSON envelope: { score: 0-1, issues: string[], recommendations: string[], extractionEligible: boolean }. The extractionEligible flag is the gate used by synthesize_template — true iff score >= qualityThreshold AND templateAuthor is not in the ribosome family. SIMPLIFICATION: a deterministic `template_quality_scorer` resolver (extracted from scoreTemplateQuality) would replace this LLM call once the scoring heuristics stabilize (post-ship ribosome extraction of THIS meta-activity itself!). For first ship the LLM is bounded at maxTokens=600. SHORT-CIRCUIT: skips when acquire_trace_signature produced no useful trace data (impulse-resolve failed OR backend unavailable) — substring-match idiom on the trace_signature impulse content for the literal `"tasks"` (every executionTraceWithSignatures result with at least one task contains this key). When the trace fetch fails the parent test/canary doesn't waste an LLM call on an empty assessment.

tasks.description: LLM renders an `extractedTemplate`-shaped JSON proposal from the trace signature + lifecycle payload.
tasks.notes: Mirrors `assembleTemplateFromExecution` in template-generator.ts:400 — extracts a template body whose tasks correspond to the trace's executed tasks, with resolver/prompt/inputShapes/outputShapes derived from the per-task signature rows. Naming: derives templateId from `learned-<short-goal-slug>-<timestamp>` (mirrors activity.ts:3554 imperative path). CONDITIONAL: fires only when assess_quality reported extractionEligible=true (substring match `"extractionEligible":true` against the quality_assessment impulse content). When the gate fails the meta-activity completes early — the trace_signature impulse is the only artefact; downstream consumers can still inspect it for failure analysis. SIMPLIFICATION: the canonical implementation would register a deterministic `template_synthesizer` resolver that maps trace signatures to canonical ActivityTemplate JSON without LLM cost (post-ship ribosome extraction); for first ship the LLM body is bounded at maxTokens=synthesisMaxTokens (default 2000). The output is an `extractedTemplate`-shape impulse (a NEW shape declared by this meta-activity for downstream replace-activity / operator consumption).

tasks.description: LLM validates the synthesized template against compliance rules.

prompt.template:
You are validating a ribosome-extracted activityTemplate proposal against compliance rules.

PROPOSAL: {{impulse:extracted_template}}

RULES:
1. id matches /^[a-z0-9-]+$/ (no whitespace, no uppercase).
2. Every task has either prompt.template OR resolver.
3. resolver field (if present) references a known resolver from this set: bash, file, git, llm, impulse-resolve, activity, validation, pattern-validator, template_sync, human, pre-validation, impulse_state_analysis, context_acquisition, failure_penalty, goal_satisfaction_checker, orchestration_goal_detector, context_template_router, keyword_extractor, impulse_cooccurrence, relevance_scorer, variant_selection, activity_recommendation, impulse_preparation, impulse_pool_selection, producer_selection, learning_signal_writer, iteration, goal_verification, ribosome, llm_impulse_selector, tool_selector, goal_enrichment, goal_decomposition, vessel-proxy. Vessel-prefixed names (e.g. concept-db:resolve_concept) also count as known.
4. tags conform to dot-separated regex /^[a-z0-9.]+$/.
5. At least one task has non-empty inputShapes AND at least one task has non-empty outputShapes.
6. metadata.author is 'ribosome-pattern'.

For each rule, emit an evidence row: { rule: <number>, passed: <bool>, message: <reason on fail, empty on pass> }.

Output EXACTLY this JSON (no markdown, no prose):
{"validator_id":"ribosome-extract::validate_proposal","passed":<bool>,"confidence":<0-1>,"evidence":[{"rule":<n>,"passed":<bool>,"message":"<...>"}]}

tasks.notes: Mirrors replace-activity.json::validate_proposals (lines 138-158). Per-rule checks: (1) id is unique-shaped (matches /^[a-z0-9-]+$/, no whitespace); (2) every task has either prompt.template OR resolver; (3) resolver field references a known resolver (matches the embedded test's KNOWN_RESOLVERS set: bash, file, git, llm, impulse-resolve, activity, validation, etc.); (4) tags conform to dot-separated regex (post-tag-format-fix) — only [a-z0-9.] allowed; (5) inputShapes / outputShapes are non-empty for at least the entry / exit tasks; (6) author is 'ribosome-pattern' (recursion-safety attribution). Output: a structured envelope with passed: true|false and per-rule evidence. SIMPLIFICATION: a deterministic `template_compliance_validator` resolver (extracted from validate-template-compliance.json's logic) would replace this LLM call once the rule set stabilizes; for first ship the LLM is bounded at maxTokens=400. The output is a validation_result-shape impulse following the unified contract — passed flag + evidence rows + validator_id.

pointer._payload_note: The extractedTemplate JSON is delivered via the inherited impulse pool (extracted_template). The activityTemplate_write resolver reads the payload from the pool when no inline payload field is set; alternatively a follow-up enhancement to impulse-resolve can accept `payload_impulse: "extracted_template"` for explicit binding. Until then the resolver's existing trace-driven path applies (see make-activity.json::extract_template for the same pattern).

tasks.notes: Shape-provenance correction (2026-04-27): split out from the previous `dispatch_write` so the trace's impulse pool reflects what was OBSERVED to be emitted, not what was DECLARED. This task ALWAYS emits a `writeAttempt`-shaped impulse describing what happened (success / failure / skipped) — gated on applyExtraction so a write actually occurs only when the variable is true. Persists the synthesized template via the `activityTemplate_write` write resolver (advertised by activity-api per docs/impulse-types/LEARNING_LOOP_WRITE_RESOLVERS.md, post auth fix). Replaces the imperative `mcp.registerTemplate(extractedTemplate)` call from activity.ts:3589, goal-processor.ts:2961/3005/3096/3145, improviser-resolver.ts:212/248. CONDITIONAL: gated on `applyExtraction` variable (default false) AND `validate_proposal` reported passed=true. The applyExtraction default of false makes first-canary-deploy observe-only — the chain emits an extractedTemplate proposal impulse for downstream consumers (workbench, replace-activity, operator) without actually writing. Once quality scoring is calibrated, applyExtraction can be flipped per-invocation OR per-vessel via the variable override. When the resolver fails (network, validation, etc.), the chain still completes — extract is best-effort; the trace records the failure_mode for ribosome itself to learn from (recursive learning loop). The pointer carries the full extractedTemplate as the payload via the `template` field; activity-api's write resolver validates structurally before persisting. NOTE: this task NEVER claims to emit `activityTemplate` — that is the responsibility of the downstream `dispatch_write_succeeded` task, which only fires when the write actually succeeded. This avoids polluting the impulse pool with a phantom `activityTemplate` shape on skipped/failed writes.

tasks.description: Shape-provenance task (2026-04-27): emit an `activityTemplate` impulse ONLY when the upstream write actually succeeded.

pointer.content: ribosome-extract: dispatch_write_succeeded — activityTemplate registered. The truthful shape is emitted here (NOT in dispatch_write_attempt) so the impulse pool reflects observed emissions, not declared intent. Downstream consumers gating on activityTemplate see this impulse only when applyExtraction=true AND the write succeeded. shapeOrigin: ribosome_extracted (set by the resolver via metadata).

tasks.notes: The conditional substring-matches the writeAttempt impulse content for a success marker (id field present + no error). When applyExtraction was false, dispatch_write_attempt was skipped → write_result impulse is absent → this task's conditional fails → no activityTemplate is registered in the pool. When applyExtraction was true but the write failed (network, 401, validation rejection), the writeAttempt impulse contains an error envelope → the conditional fails → again no activityTemplate. Only when a real registered template exists on the backend does this task fire and emit the truthful `activityTemplate` shape. This is the registry-quality posture: declared output shapes match observed emissions; downstream consumers (workbench, dashboards, learning-signal writers) gating on `metadata.shape: "activityTemplate"` only see the shape when a real template was actually written. The `ribosome_extracted` shapeOrigin marker (set by the resolver via metadata) makes the trace queryable: 'show me all activityTemplate impulses that came from a ribosome extraction'.

tasks.description: Emits a `learningSummary` + `goalEnd` impulse summarising the ribosome run.
tasks.notes: Conditional on assess_quality having actually produced output (substring-match on `quality_assessment` impulse) — when the upstream chain short-circuited (no trace data), the summary is skipped to avoid an LLM call with empty inputs. Mirrors make-activity.json::declare_complete (line 174-208). For mature canary use, downstream consumers (workbench history panel, dashboards) consume learningSummary to render the ribosome's learning trail per execution. The summary aggregates: trace_signature presence, quality_assessment fields (score, extractionEligible, issues, recommendations), extracted_template id+name (when synthesized), proposal_validation passed flag, write_result status (when dispatched), AND the registered_template impulse (only present when the write succeeded — observable shape provenance). The chain's value comes from the LLM seeing the full picture; with empty inputs there's nothing useful to summarise. The summary's `writeSucceeded` boolean is now driven by the presence of the `registered_template` impulse rather than parsing the writeAttempt envelope — observable rather than declared.

metadata.author: ribosome-pattern
supersedes: goal-processor.ts:2993-3016 cost-limit attempt extraction (removed; out-of-scope: requires lifecycle:activity:failure subscriber)
goal-processor.ts:3128-3156 max-turns attempt extraction (removed; out-of-scope: requires lifecycle:activity:failure subscriber)
openQuestions: FAILURE-PATH RIBOSOME (cost-limit, max-turns): the imperative path also extracted ATTEMPT templates from cost-exhausted and max-turns improvisations via `extractAttemptTemplate`. The current meta-activity subscribes to lifecycle:activity:postExecution which fires on completed AND per-task-failed activities, but the improviser cost-limit/max-turns paths terminate WITHOUT firing postExecution (they go through `convertImprovisationToExecution` and return directly). A sibling subscriber on lifecycle:activity:failure (or a new lifecycle:activity:improviserExhausted event) is the proper fix; deferred until the improviser-driven failure path is wired through the executor's lifecycle emit machinery. Until then attempt-template extraction is OUT OF SCOPE — the meta-activity only handles the success path that the imperative code's three success sites previously covered (activity.ts, goal-processor success, goal-processor LLM-verified, improviser success).

TEMPLATE-PAYLOAD SYNTHESIS (synthesize_template + dispatch_write): the LLM body in synthesize_template renders a structurally-valid ActivityTemplate JSON; activity-api's `activityTemplate_write` resolver validates structurally before persisting (post auth fix). SIMPLIFICATION: a deterministic `template_synthesizer` resolver (extracted from `assembleTemplateFromExecution` in template-generator.ts:400) would replace the LLM call once the synthesis pattern stabilizes — POST-SHIP RIBOSOME EXTRACTION OF THIS META-ACTIVITY ITSELF (a recursive learning loop). For first ship the LLM is bounded at maxTokens=synthesisMaxTokens (default 2000).

QUALITY SCORER (assess_quality): the LLM-based scorer is a low-cost placeholder — a deterministic `template_quality_scorer` resolver (extracted from `scoreTemplateQuality` in template-generator.ts:885) would replace this LLM call once enough scoring traces accumulate for ribosome extraction. Until then the LLM is bounded at maxTokens=600.

RECURSION-SAFETY VIA TEMPLATEAUTHOR: the meta-activity's gate is templateAuthor != 'ribosome' && != 'ribosome-pattern' && != 'ribosome-sequence' (mirrors activity.ts:3525-3526 imperative skip). A more rigorous fix would use the static-mutual-recursion check in templates.test.ts (Tier 4) — but Tier 4 only catches output_shape collisions, not author-driven skips. The current author-string match relies on the synthesize_template prompt instructing the LLM to set metadata.author to 'ribosome-pattern' (the canonical attribution); if the LLM violates this contract, validate_proposal's rule 6 catches it before dispatch_write fires.

COMPOSITION-EDGE RECORDING: the imperative path also called `mcp.recordComposition()` (activity.ts:3598-3618) to record the parent → child composition edge after successful registration. The meta-activity does NOT currently record this edge — the `activityTemplate_write` resolver may handle it server-side OR a follow-up sibling task could invoke a `compositionEdge_write` resolver. Tracked as a follow-up cleanup pass.

BOREDOM-QUEUE ENQUEUE: the imperative path also enqueued the new template for boredom-queue testing (activity.ts:3629-3645). The meta-activity does NOT currently enqueue — boredom-queue enqueueing is a separate concern and could be a sibling subscriber on the `activityTemplate_write_result` shape. Tracked as a follow-up cleanup pass.
limitations: Failure-path ribosome (cost-limit, max-turns) is OUT OF SCOPE; only success-path extraction is covered. Sibling subscriber on lifecycle:activity:failure is the proper fix.
synthesize_template uses LLM-based template synthesis (not a deterministic template_synthesizer); bounded by synthesisMaxTokens. Deterministic synthesizer is a follow-up.
assess_quality uses LLM-based quality scoring (not a deterministic template_quality_scorer); bounded by maxTokens=600.

Recursion safety relies on templateAuthor string-matching the ribosome family. The synthesize_template prompt instructs the LLM to set author='ribosome-pattern'; validate_proposal rule 6 catches violations before write.
applyExtraction defaults to false — first canary deploy is observe-only. Flip to true once quality calibration converges OR per-invocation via variable override.
Composition-edge recording (parent → extracted child) is NOT done by this meta-activity; tracked as follow-up.
Boredom-queue enqueue of the extracted template is NOT done; tracked as follow-up.

dispatch_write_succeeded uses substring-match on the writeAttempt impulse content for an `id` field as the success signal. Activity-api's write resolver returns the registered template's id field on success and an error envelope on failure; the substring approach is the same idiom used by slot-binding.json (line 162) and goal-processing-activity-driven.json (line 162). Once a deterministic gate primitive lands the conditional can be tightened; until then this is the proven pattern.
metadata.outputContract: Truthful output-shape contract per shape-provenance correction (2026-04-27): emissions reflect what was OBSERVED to happen, not what was DECLARED. (1) Always emits a `learningSummary` and `goalEnd` impulse via emit_summary (mandatory regardless of applyExtraction OR quality verdict, gated only on having quality_assessment data). (2) When qualityEligible AND quality_score >= threshold, ALSO emits an `extractedTemplate` proposal impulse via synthesize_template. (3) When applyExtraction=true (regardless of write outcome), ALSO emits a `writeAttempt`-shaped impulse via dispatch_write_attempt — describes what was attempted and the resolver's response (success/error envelope). (4) When applyExtraction=true AND the write succeeded (writeAttempt content has an `id` field), ALSO emits an `activityTemplate` impulse via dispatch_write_succeeded — the truthful counterpart to a registered template, NOT a phantom emission on skipped/failed writes. Dynamic shapes (validation_result, executionTraceWithSignatures) flow through the existing nested-execution merge path. The shape-provenance discipline: an `activityTemplate` impulse appears in the pool ONLY when a real backend-registered template exists; consumers gating on it (workbench, dashboards) can rely on this without parsing metadata.error / metadata.degraded.
metadata.subscriberContract: subscription.shape = 'lifecycle:activity:postExecution'. Fires after every activity execution's trace storage (activity.ts:3680+, post-2026-04-27 ribosome refactor). Lifecycle payload: { executionId, templateId, templateName, templateAuthor, status, durationMs, costUsd, taskCount, impulseCount, depth, compositionChain, outputShapes, hasGoalContext, qualityEligible }. The dotted-path interpolator JSON-stringifies array values when embedded as resolver-config string leaves; the impulse-resolve resolver tolerates JSON-stringified array forms. Subscriber outputs (extractedTemplate, learningSummary, validation_result, activityTemplate_write_result, goalEnd) merge back into the parent execution's impulse pool via the existing nested-execution machinery (activity.ts:1249-1273) — though for postExecution the parent is already finalised, so subscriber outputs surface in the trace as a child execution under composition_chain.
metadata.spec_reference: ribosome-as-meta-activity refactor (2026-04-27). Architectural change: imperative inline ribosome calls → declarative lifecycle-subscribed meta-activity, mirroring slot-binding / validator-dispatch / create-shape-provider-goal pattern. Treats template extraction as a shape-identifying counterpart to goal/activity (input shape: lifecycle:activity:postExecution, output shape: extractedTemplate). Quality gating moved from code (activity.ts:3586 `qualityResult.score >= 0.6`) to template variable (qualityThreshold default 0.7). Write path moved from MCP client (mcp.registerTemplate) to activityTemplate_write resolver (post auth fix). The applyExtraction=false default makes first-canary observe-only (proposal-emit) before any writes happen.
metadata._design_intent: Per the user framing (2026-04-27): 'ribosome itself ought to be another activity driven resolver and we should treat it like a shape identifying counterpart to goal/activity that runs after execution and is registered to the lifecycle hook.' This template realizes that intent. The meta-activity's role: identify the `extractedTemplate` shape — the ribosome's output is a NEW activity, just as goal-processing's output is a goal-shaped impulse. The lifecycle hook (postExecution) is the trigger; the chain is observable, gateable, and Thompson-Sampling-rankable like any other meta-activity.
